newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crudes firm, Australian fields to shut again.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes firm, Australian fields to shut again.

text.p: Crude prices in Asia were steady to firmer on Monday, with light sweet grades underpinned by expectations of further Australian shut-downs owing to storms.
Operators of both the 90,000 barrels per day (bpd) Cossack and 70,000 bpd Griffin offshore fields said they planned to shut down operators owing to the approaching Cyclone Rachel.
Both fields were shut down for much of last week owing to a separate cyclone.
Barrow Island and Thevenard were also considering shutting in production, the fields' operator said. The shut downs would cut potentially about 200,000 bpd production from the market.

Traders said the news underpinned Tapis paper, where January was bid at $25.25 per barrel with a notional offer around $25.50, steady with Friday despite a fall in Brent and NYMEX futures over the weekend.
A producer said he was seeking a premium of $1.70 for February barrels. He said he was seeing interest to buy from Thailand and Singapore.
Official selling prices from Oman and ADNOC showed a widening of their premiums over the monthly average Dubai price.
Middle East crudes achieved strong premiums in trading for February, which had translated into the wider spreads for March.
Traders said spot availability in 1997 was little changed from 1996, but higher crude processing capacity, refiners maximising runs and China looking to replenish stocks was supporting the market.
One trader said Oman's differential to Dubai stretched to $1.04 from 86 cents, after February premiums hit 30 cents plus.
The trader said a 10-cent premium for Oman was achievable for March trading.
